title: Things to Do in Gangtok: MG Marg, Monasteries, Viewpoints & Day Trips
seoTitle: Things to Do in Gangtok: Monasteries, Views & More | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Gangtok: MG Marg, Rumtek and Enchey monasteries, the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, Do Drul Chorten, the ropeway, Tashi View Point, Ganesh Tok and Hanuman Tok, Banjhakri Falls, and day trips to Tsomgo Lake, Nathula and Rumtek.
dek: Sikkim's clean, hill-hugging capital, with a pedestrian high street, Buddhist monasteries on the ridges and Kanchenjunga on the horizon.
searchIntent: Travellers spending two to three days in Gangtok, often while arranging permits for Tsomgo, Nathula and North Sikkim.
intro: Gangtok, the capital of Sikkim, is built along a steep ridge at about 1,650 metres, with the Ranikhola valley below and Kanchenjunga visible on clear days. It is a small, orderly city, known for its clean streets, its pedestrian MG Marg and its mix of Buddhist, Hindu and Nepali cultures.

The things to do in Gangtok include monasteries such as Rumtek and Enchey, the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, viewpoints around the ridge, a cable car ride, evenings on MG Marg and day trips to Tsomgo Lake and Nathula Pass. It is also where travellers arrange permits for North Sikkim.
Two to three days is ideal. March to June and September to December are the best months.
quickAnswer: Stroll MG Marg in the evening
Visit the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Do Drul Chorten
See Kanchenjunga from Tashi View Point
Visit Ganesh Tok and Hanuman Tok
Take a day trip to Tsomgo Lake and Nathula

items.name: Stroll MG Marg
body: Mahatma Gandhi Marg is Gangtok's pedestrian high street, lined with shops, cafés and restaurants, with benches and flower beds down the middle. Smoking, littering and spitting are prohibited, and the street stays remarkably clean. It is liveliest in the evening.

items.name: Visit the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology
body: The Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, founded in 1958, is a research centre with a museum of Buddhist icons, thangkas, manuscripts and ritual objects. Nearby, Do Drul Chorten is a large white stupa ringed by prayer wheels, built in 1945.

items.name: See Enchey Monastery
body: Enchey Monastery, above the city, belongs to the Nyingma school and is about 200 years old in its origins; the current building dates from 1909. Its annual cham dance takes place in winter.

items.name: Ride the ropeway
body: The Gangtok ropeway runs between Deorali and the Secretariat area, giving views of the city and valley. It is a short ride, and queues can be long at weekends.

items.name: See Tsuklakhang
body: Tsuklakhang, the former royal chapel next to the old palace, is where Sikkim's kings were crowned and married. It is the venue for major festival dances such as Pang Lhabsol; at other times, access may be limited, so ask locally.

items.name: See Kanchenjunga from Tashi View Point
body: Tashi View Point, on the road north of the city, offers views of Kanchenjunga and the surrounding peaks on clear mornings. Ganesh Tok and Hanuman Tok, small hilltop temples, give different views over Gangtok and the ranges.

items.name: See Banjhakri Falls
body: Banjhakri Falls and Energy Park, a few kilometres from the city, is a landscaped park around a waterfall, with statues depicting the shamanic tradition of the jhakri. It is popular with families.

items.name: Visit the Flower Exhibition Centre
body: The Flower Exhibition Centre near the Ridge Park shows orchids and seasonal flowers, especially in spring. Sikkim has hundreds of orchid species.

items.name: Visit Rumtek Monastery
body: Rumtek, about 24 km from Gangtok, is the largest monastery in Sikkim and was rebuilt in the 1960s as the seat of the Karmapa of the Karma Kagyu school after he left Tibet. Its main hall, golden stupa and courtyard are impressive. Security checks apply and ID may be needed.

items.name: Go to Tsomgo Lake and Nathula
body: Tsomgo Lake, about 38 km away at 3,750 metres, is a glacial lake with yaks, snow and mountain views. With a permit and on permitted days, Indian nationals can continue to Nathula Pass on the India–China border and the Baba Harbhajan Singh Mandir. Permits are arranged through registered agents, usually a day in advance.

items.name: Arrange a North Sikkim trip
body: From Gangtok, two- to three-day packages go to Lachung and Yumthang Valley, and to Lachen and Gurudongmar Lake. Permits, vehicles and stays are arranged together. Check road status, as landslides can close routes.

items.name: See Hanuman Tok and Ganesh Tok
body: Hanuman Tok, a temple on a hill above the city maintained by the Indian Army, is one of the best places near Gangtok to see Kanchenjunga at sunrise. Ganesh Tok, a tiny shrine on a ridge closer to town, has a viewing platform over the city. Both are usually combined with Tashi View Point on a morning sightseeing loop.

items.name: Visit the Himalayan Zoological Park
body: The Himalayan Zoological Park at Bulbuley, next to Ganesh Tok, keeps red pandas, Himalayan black bears, snow leopards and other mountain animals in large forested enclosures along a walking or driving loop.

items.name: See the Ridge Park and White Hall
body: The Ridge, above MG Marg, is a shaded walkway past the Palace gates and White Hall, a colonial building. In spring, the flower show at the Ridge brings orchids and seasonal blooms.

items.name: Visit Lingdum (Ranka) Monastery
body: Lingdum Monastery at Ranka, about 20 km from Gangtok, is a large, relatively new monastery with a spacious courtyard, forested surroundings and a calm atmosphere. Morning prayers are a good time to visit.

items.name: Drive to Seven Sisters Falls and Tashi View Point
body: On the road towards North Sikkim, Seven Sisters Waterfall near Gangtok is a roadside cascade that is at its fullest after the monsoon. It is often a stop on the way to Lachung.

items.name: Eat Sikkimese and Tibetan food
body: Gangtok has many small restaurants serving momos, thukpa, phagshapa, sha phaley and gundruk soup. Try local teas and, if you drink, local millet beer.

items.name: Shop at Lal Bazaar and the handicraft centre
body: Lal Bazaar, below MG Marg, is the local market for vegetables, spices, chhurpi and household goods. The Directorate of Handicrafts and Handloom sells carpets, thangkas, masks and woodwork made by local artisans.

items.name: Losar, Saga Dawa and Pang Lhabsol
body: Losar, the Tibetan new year in February or March, brings monastery prayers and masked dances. Saga Dawa in late spring features processions with scriptures through Gangtok. Pang Lhabsol in late summer honours Kanchenjunga with warrior dances at Tsuklakhang, the former royal chapel. Dates follow the lunar calendar.

items.name: The Red Panda Winter Carnival
body: Gangtok's winter carnival, usually held in December, brings food stalls, music and cultural performances to MG Marg and makes an otherwise quiet season lively.

byTraveller.text: MG Marg, the ropeway, Banjhakri Falls and a Tsomgo day trip for snow.
Sunrise at Tashi View Point, a Rumtek visit and evenings at MG Marg's cafés.
Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, Rumtek, Enchey and the handicraft centre.

oneDay: Start with sunrise at Tashi View Point, then visit Ganesh Tok and Hanuman Tok. Visit Enchey Monastery and the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology before lunch. In the afternoon, drive to Rumtek, then return for the ropeway and an evening on MG Marg.
tips: Bagdogra Airport is about four to five hours away; Pakyong Airport has limited flights.
Shared jeeps and taxis are the main transport; there are no app cabs in most areas.
Arrange Tsomgo, Nathula and North Sikkim permits through registered agents in advance.
Carry ID; checkposts and some monasteries ask for it.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Gangtok?
faqs.a: Walk MG Marg, visit Rumtek and Enchey monasteries, see the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, ride the ropeway, visit viewpoints such as Tashi View Point and Ganesh Tok, and take a day trip to Tsomgo Lake and Nathula.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Gangtok?
faqs.a: Two to three days for the city and Tsomgo, plus two or three more for North Sikkim.

faqs.q: Can I visit Nathula Pass from Gangtok?
faqs.a: Yes, Indian nationals can visit with a permit on permitted days. Foreign nationals are not allowed at Nathula.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Gangtok?
faqs.a: March to June and September to December.

faqs.q: Is Gangtok good for a family holiday?
faqs.a: Yes. MG Marg, the ropeway, the zoo, Banjhakri Falls and a Tsomgo Lake day trip for snow suit families well.
